kind: re-measurement of the AuRUS baseline arm alone, at an output-only fork
kind_note: No PEREDUR search ran here. The PEREDUR side of every contrast is 2026-09-14-paper-rerun's nsga2-apportion/mrs cell, closed on 2026-09-18. The scoring of this arm is two further campaigns, 2026-09-22-aurus-rerun-curves (separation and maximality) and 2026-09-23-aurus-rerun-anytime (per-solution anytime verdicts and the well-separation screen), each with its own archive.
question: Whether the paper's AuRUS column survives once AuRUS stops losing the solutions of a run killed at the 7200 s cap, and what its anytime figures become when each solution is dated by the tool's own microsecond clock.
method: Recorded at run time, not reconstructed. The arm ran as a `kind = "aurus"` phase of the campaign.toml archived beside this file, staged to both hosts through scripts/campaign.py, which verified the AuRUS commit against each host's COMMIT.txt before launch and again in the runner before the first JVM started. Run window, counts, flags and concurrency are read from aurus-manifest-<host>.json; per-run and per-family figures from aurus_results-<host>.csv and aurus-adapt-<host>.json; the decision from analysis-output.txt. On 2026-10-01 all six data files here were checked by md5sum against the copies on av2 and av3 and are identical.

aurus.what_changed: Output alone, per PLAN.md section 2. Upstream writes ga.solutions in one batch after the search loop, so a run killed at the cap loses everything with the JVM, and it dates a solution from the run log's per-iteration #Sol column, rounded to the second. The fork writes each solution as it is found and appends its elapsed time to solution-times.csv to the microsecond.

registered_primary.largest_differences: PEREDUR ahead on full-arbiter-aurus and prioritized-arbiter-aurus (+0.667 each, AuRUS 0 of 30 on both), and by +0.133 on humanoid-531, lily02 and load-balancer-aurus; behind on gyro-var2 (-0.500), lily11 (-0.433) and lift (-0.333).
registered_primary.aurus_rates_unscreened: analyse_matched prints AuRUS's per-family rates unfiltered by the well-separation screen. The paper applies the screen downstream through prepare.py; the registered test does not.

registered_secondary.definition: PLAN.md section 4: the same test restricted to the families whose archived repeats were never censored. analyse_matched does not print it; its printed `scorable runs only` read is the rematch's secondary and appears below for completeness.
registered_secondary.computed: On 2026-10-01 from the per-family table in analysis-output.txt's REGISTERED PRIMARY section, with wilcoxon_exact_p from scripts/analyse_matched.py, differences taken as (PEREDUR hits - AuRUS hits) / 30.
registered_secondary.count_note: PLAN.md says 20 families. It counted 26 minus the six censored families, but humanoid-741 is outside the 25, and the archive also killed one lily02 repeat, so strictly 19 of the 25 were never censored. Both reads are null.

decision_rule: PLAN.md section 5. Outcome 1, PEREDUR higher at p < 0.05: PEREDUR ahead. Outcome 2, AuRUS higher at p < 0.05: reported as measured and RQ1 rewritten. Outcome 3, null: parity, with the discordant counts. In every outcome the paper reports the archive's censoring, this campaign replaces it, and a supersession row naming 2026-08-14-aurus-h2h goes in experiments/README.md.
decision: Outcome 3, null, reported as parity: PEREDUR higher on 12 families, lower on 8, tied on 5, mean difference +0.012, exact two-sided Wilcoxon p = 0.7214. The registered secondary is null too, p = 0.3369 over the plan's 20 families and p = 0.2235 over the 19 strictly never censored. This arm supersedes 2026-08-14-aurus-h2h as the project's AuRUS measurement, and the supersession row is in experiments/README.md as of this close.
decision_caveat_float_ties: wilcoxon_exact_p receives differences of float rates, and signed_ranks groups ties with ==, so equal differences reached by different float paths (0.0333...326 against 0.0333...333, 0.0666...665 against 0.0666...667, 0.1333...33 against 0.1333...333, 0.1999...96 against 0.2000...07) rank apart. On exact differences the registered p is 0.7348 rather than 0.7214, the 20-family secondary 0.3369 rather than 0.3370 and the 19-family one 0.2235 rather than 0.2224. No outcome moves. The registered figure is the analyser's printed 0.7214; the defect is in analyse_matched.py at 57fcefb and was not fixed here.

caveats: The PEREDUR arm is not re-run here. It is 2026-09-14-paper-rerun's, run at 57fcefb eight days earlier. PLAN.md section 6 registers this.
Every recovered run sits in the six capped families. A swing must be read per family rather than pooled.

15 runs that were not killed produced nothing: detector-aurus 0, gyro-var1 0, 15 and 24, gyro-var2 21, humanoid-503 15, lift 15, lily02 0, lily16 15, load-balancer-aurus 14, ltl2dba-theta-2 15 and 26, prioritized-arbiter-aurus 5, rg1 0 and simple-arbiter-aurus 3. Each exited 0 with aurus_time_s 0, and each run.log on the hosts reads `Initial specification is: unknown` and then `The specification is inconsistent`. The one read in full, detector-aurus repeat 0, first prints SAT-solver warnings of a DIMACS header mismatch. 9 of the 15 are repeat 0 or repeat 15, the first of a host's split. The cause was not investigated, and they score as failures in every read.

peak_rss_mb does not measure the JVM. Its maximum over all 780 rows is 3.5 MB against an 8 GB heap reservation, and it reads 0.0 on 14 of the 15 quick exits, so the sampler read some other process. No memory figure in this arm is usable.

An implication that times out reads as a non-implication, so every ideal count is a lower bound. On humanoid-742 the anytime pass recorded compare's `timeout` verdict for 18,574 of 18,988 solutions (2026-09-23-aurus-rerun-anytime).
Concurrency rose from 10 to 14 against the archive. Wall time is not an endpoint here.
